-------------------------
= Introduction =
-------------------------

Robinviz is implemented using both python( where we require PyQT and Python) and C( where we use C++ library LEDA and C++ compiler). Simply, the data retrieval processes are handled in Robinviz Graphical User Interface(GUI) using PyQT and Python. Remaining concepts and data usage are coded using C and Leda C++ library. Robinviz has several features hence makes the tool complicated. So, we try to follow and report errors. In case of unreported errors, you can follow the execution at the console and even you can inform us.

Although we present binary packages for Linux and Windows operating systems, programmers can recompile and use the existing implementation. Through the manual, we first show source code compilation in both Linux( valid for well used distributions) and Windows. Then, we introduce GUI. Finally, we demonstrate a sample run for the first time users.

-------------------------
= Compilation =
-------------------------

== @ Linux ==

===Requirements===

LEDA 5.1+ Library from Algorithmic Solutions
libX11-dev
g++


===Steps===

# Add the following lines to your `~/.bashrc`

{{{
export LEDAROOT=/path/to/LEDA
export PATH=$PATH:$LEDAROOT/Manual/cmd
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:$LEDAROOT
}}}

Make sure that incl folder is inside this LEDA_ROOT.

# Give the following command on console,

{{{
source ~/.bashrc
}}}

# Move to the robinviz directory on console and give the following command:

{{{
sh compile.sh
}}}

All the executables should be compiled.

== @ Windows ==

===Requirements===

LEDA 5.1+ Library from Algorithmic Solutions
Visual Studio 2005 C++ or over

===Steps===

1. Follow the instruction given at http://www.algorithmicsolutions.info/leda_manual/DLL_s_MS_Visual.html

or

1. Shall use sample Visual Studio 2005 Solution Template located at the main source distribution folder.
2. Setup LEDA 5.1+ Library from Algorithmic Solutions
3. Follow the instruction given at http://www.algorithmic-solutions.info/leda_manual/DLL_s_MS_Visual.html or if you use the template, you will need to 
add library path and include folder from menu bar Tools->Options->Project and Solutions->VC++ Directories.

== Central Visualizations ==

We now introduce the GUI of Robinviz. We take all screenshots using the svn version 298.

If you double click on "robinviz.exe" in windows or run the command "./robinviz.exe", you shall see the following empty screen.

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/1_first_time_opening.png||
|| When you open robinviz first time, you see this blank view ||

Next, in order to view the visualizations, you are required to follow input operations where is at the File menu and then you are required to click "File>Run(Ctrl+R)". On the other hand, if you desire to see the last session or previous sessions, you can load your last session by pressing "Ctrl+E" or "File>Display Recent Results", also, loadin previous sessions can be done via clicking on "File>load session" option. After, you are done with one of these three options, you simply see the following snapshot.

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/2_after_execution.png||
|| Snaphsot after run or any load operation with Central View||

You now have graph at the center where we call "Central View" and search box;

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_2_after_clicks.png

Robinviz has 16 empty screen views where we call them as "Peripheral Views", arround the "Central View" and a three tabbed search box. Using the search box, you can click and see "Central View" nodes and their labels from while "Cat" is on clicked. You can also query for proteins and observe the categories, that have the query protein, while "Pro" is on clicked. 

|| http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/4_2_category_search_box.png || http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/3_2_protein_search_box.png ||
|| Search Box for Categories(Co-ontology) or Biclusters(Co-Expression) ||  Search Box for proteins ||

Next, at the previous screenshot, you see the empty 16 screens. These screens are interactive and respond when you click on nodes(Categories,Biclusters) in "Central View". At each clicking on nodes, you shall see that a new graph appears at these empty screens. When you click 16 different nodes, you should obtain a similar snapshot;

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_after_clicks.png ||
|| When you fill 16 peripheral screens. ||

We call all these 16 views as "Peripheral Views";

http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/5_1_after_clicks.png

where you see the Protein-Protein Interaction sub network created via proteins of the clicked category node.

In Robinviz we have also, some supporting tables and visualizations. Since we process over Gene Ontology categories, we form a table where we show each genes/proteins belongs to which categories as well. The following screen shows this table;

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/6_go_view.png ||
|| GO Table when you right click on nodes and select "Go Table" or when you right click anywhere of "Peripheral View" and again select "Go Table"||

If you right click on "Central View", you are allowed to see severak other options. You may open the view in a new window for clear visibility, print the visualization, save the graph of visualization in GML format and try another layouts. For example, if you try our "Spring Embedder on Circular Tracks" for "Central View", the layout changes with nice animation.

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/7_run_layout.png ||
|| Sample demonstration of "Spring Embedder on Circular Tracks" for "Central View" ||

We should now be comfortable with main visualization screen. We now show how peripheral visualizations works.

== Peripheral Visualizations ==

For "Peripheral Views", we have new options and inhereted options from "Central View". In "Peripheral Views", you now see proteins. We mention that you can click on nodes inside "Central View" and each nodes appears as a peripheral view around the "Central View". When you right click over
the first peripheral view and select "Open in a new Window". Robinviz creates another window and show larger snapshot of clicked peripheral view.

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/8_open_peripherals.png ||
|| A peripheral view opened with a new window ||

Similarly, you can change layouts in that windows as well. For example, if you run "Spring Embedder", you will have,

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/9_protein_screen_1.png ||
|| A peripheral view after "Spring Embedder"||

You are allowed to open any peripheral views with a new window. In "Peripheral View", we have also one more option that you can do just using mouse clicks. Each protein nodes in "Peripheral View" allows you to right click on it and shows a popup menu.
In that popup menu, you have two options; "Get Information about the selected protein from Biogrid website", "See original sub network with one hop neighborhood" and "two hop neighborhood.
If you select to see "Two hop neigborhood", you complete three level views of Robinviz and the snapshot is as follows;

||http://robinviz.googlecode.com/svn/manual/images/10_three_level_view.png ||
|| Central View at the background, a peripheral view on the left, a clicked node from peripheral view and its two hop neighborhood at the right ||

Particularly, we complete the important GUI operations for Robinviz. However, to have well understanding, we present a real case scenario at the next section.
